sections.title: Complete this brand-to-call approval sheet
paragraphs:

| Instruction | Exact material to confirm | Who must answer the approval question? | What stays unresolved until confirmed? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Business identity | Approved trading name and opening greeting | Franchisee and applicable brand contact | Whether the proposed introduction may be used |
| Service descriptions | Wording for the residential work this unit offers | The person responsible for approved service information | Whether the handler may describe an unfamiliar service |
| Promotions and fees | Current wording, dates and exceptions | The authorized offer owner | Any promise absent from the approved instruction |
| Appointment language | Request wording versus a supported confirmation | Local scheduling owner and any required brand reviewer | Whether a requested time has actually been accepted |

sections.title: Separate the franchisee's decision from the provider's configuration
paragraphs:

sections.title: Request a demonstration of one approved change and one exception
paragraphs:

Ask how the provider handles an edit awaiting approval, a conflicting instruction and a recipient who cannot take a transfer. Record the observed outcome and the remaining question; do not assume an approval workflow or version-control feature exists inside the product.

sections.title: Compare offers on the approved scope
paragraphs:
[MAP's franchise service page](https://www.mapcommunications.com/industries/franchises/) describes branded live answering and customized scripts for franchise buyers. That supports asking for a franchise-specific proposal; it does not establish approval for your franchise or verify a provider's performance.

For Revo, evaluate its published AI answering, business-script intake, supported appointment booking and call summaries. Team transfers depend on the selected plan and supported configuration. Confirm those details against [current Revo plans](/pricing).

This guide establishes no Revo franchisor console, centralized brand-approval workflow, human receptionist network or franchise-system endorsement. If one of those is essential, obtain evidence of a suitable arrangement before buying. For branch accounts and billing, use the separate [multi-location pricing guide](/ai-answering-service/multi-location-answering-service-pricing); this page addresses permission to use and change the caller-facing instructions.

sections.title: Questions before buying
paragraphs:
### Does an answering provider's franchise page prove my franchise permits it?

No. Confirm the requirement through your actual documents and authorized franchise contact. The provider's marketing describes its offer, not your permission to purchase it.

### Can the receptionist decide whether a promotion or warranty applies?

Only use the authority and accepted instructions established for the task. Where an authorized person must decide, collect the request and direct it to that owner.

### Must I operate several locations to use this worksheet?

No. One franchisee can need brand-approved wording even for one local business. That is separate from comparing multiple accounts, locations or invoices.

### Is this a franchise agreement checklist?

No. It is an operational sheet for identifying the accepted caller-facing instructions and the people responsible for them. It does not decide contractual rights or replace qualified document review.

[Review Revo's current reception plans](/pricing) after identifying the approval questions and the incoming-call tasks your local business needs covered.

record.description: Compare CMS answering coverage using its quoted billing period, included minutes and HVAC handoff scope. Separate reception from dispatch before choosing.
record.lead: Continental Message Solution, or CMS, offers live answering alongside a broader call-center service catalog. A US residential HVAC business comparing it with an AI receptionist should first confirm two things: the billing period in its actual quote and the work the selected service is authorized to complete.
record.intro: Continental Message Solution, or CMS, offers live answering alongside a broader call-center service catalog. A US residential HVAC business comparing it with an AI receptionist should first confirm two things: the billing period in its actual quote and the work the selected service is authorized to complete.

sections.title: Resolve the period before using a monthly budget
paragraphs:
The [CMS pricing page](https://www.continentalmessage.com/pricing/) introduces plans with “$50/month,” while its plan cards display prices per 28 days. Treat that difference as a question for the written proposal rather than silently changing either label.

These are the displayed cards reviewed on that date, not a complete account-specific tariff:

| Published card | Displayed recurring amount | Displayed included minutes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry / PAYG | $50 per 28 days | None |
| Starter | $150 per 28 days | 100 |
| Small Biz | $300 per 28 days | 250 |
| Standard | $575 per 28 days | 500 |

The same page offers custom quotes, says setup depends on account complexity, and directs buyers to obtain the selected plan's additional-minute rate. The entry amount is therefore not evidence of a complete bill or included call handling at no usage charge.

A 28-day period is four weeks; it is not a calendar month. Ask for the start date, reset dates and invoice schedule that would apply to your account. Compare providers over the same explicit dates and workload. Do not multiply every displayed period price by twelve and label the result a comparable annual cost.

sections.title: Use this quote-normalization sheet
paragraphs:
Complete one column for each actual proposal. An unanswered field remains unknown, not zero. This worksheet is an original purchasing resource, not a CMS or Revo billing feature.

| Field | What to obtain before comparing |
| --- | --- |
| Selected offer | Exact plan name, dated proposal and accepted service scope |
| Period | Start and end dates, reset rule and recurring invoice schedule |
| Included usage | Allowance, unit and treatment of unused allowance |
| Chargeable activity | Written definitions for conversations, hold time, transfers and other billed work |
| Additional usage | Applicable rate, rounding and the activity to which it applies |
| Setup and changes | Quoted initial work and later configuration-change charges, if any |
| Retained work | Decisions and follow-up still owned by your office |

Use an authorized, anonymized record of the calls you want handled. Keep a quiet period and a busy period separate. If one quote bills minutes and another uses calls, obtain the applicable definitions before treating either total as a comparable quantity.

The [answering-service cost guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-cost) provides the broader billing-model comparison. Here, the specific issue is reconciling CMS's displayed period labels with the account proposal and its included work.

sections.title: Separate HVAC reception from dispatch and support
paragraphs:
The [CMS HVAC page](https://www.continentalmessage.com/industries/hvac/) describes scripted incoming-call handling and also markets scheduling, dispatch and customer support. Those descriptions establish what the provider advertises, not which functions your selected plan includes or how a connection to your systems would work.

Ask for a separate answer for each requested outcome. Receiving a homeowner's service inquiry is different from assigning a technician. Recording a preferred visit time is different from confirming a supported booking. Passing a message to an on-call contact is different from establishing that someone accepted the work.

Build the proposal around the outcome you need, then identify the required access, responsible business role and completion evidence. If dispatch or account research is essential, have CMS identify the corresponding scope in writing. Do not assume it is included because an adjacent page describes it.

Keep technical advice, safety decisions and commitments about field attendance with the appropriate authorized people. This guide supplies no HVAC diagnosis or emergency procedure.

sections.title: Test the office handoff before routing customer calls
paragraphs:
Request a provider-authorized demonstration using three fictional requests: a new service inquiry, an existing customer's visit question and a request for a person who is unavailable. Inspect the record your office would receive and who would own the next action.

For a proposed booking, check which system is authoritative and what establishes confirmation. For a proposed transfer, check the unavailable-recipient outcome. Where the demonstration requires a software connection, verify that specific arrangement; a list of supported products is not evidence that your account has been configured or tested.

Keep the billing question alongside the observed workflow. A useful operational result and a clearly defined charging unit are both needed to assess the proposal. Neither a successful sample call nor a low starting amount establishes the full service you would receive.

sections.title: Compare Revo on its actual answering scope
paragraphs:
Revo publishes AI answering, business-script intake, supported appointment booking and call summaries. Team transfers depend on the selected plan and supported configuration. Review [current Revo plans](/pricing) for the incoming-call tasks your business needs.

This article establishes no Revo live-agent staffing, technician-dispatch service, CMS portal connection, help desk, employee hotline or mass-notification program. If you need one of those functions, evaluate a suitable separately verified arrangement. Compare a Revo reception plan with the reception portion of a CMS proposal rather than treating the entire CMS catalog as an equivalent subscription.

sections.title: Questions before choosing
paragraphs:
### Is Continental Message Solution the same provider as the plural search phrase?

This guide identifies the business at continentalmessage.com, which uses Continental Message Solution and CMS. Confirm the provider identity and proposal sender before relying on a similarly named search result.

### Does the $50 entry card include minutes?

The reviewed CMS card says no included minutes. Obtain the usage rate, definitions and other applicable charges before estimating an actual bill.

### Can I compare a 28-day quote directly with a calendar-month plan?

First align the dates, allowance resets and workload. Different periods can cover different activity; the headline recurring amounts alone are not a like-for-like comparison.

### Does the HVAC page prove dispatch is included in every CMS plan?

No. Ask which outcome, access and responsibilities the selected written offer includes. Keep unsupported or unanswered requirements visible.

[Review Revo's current plans](/pricing) and compare the verified reception scope using a completed quote-normalization sheet.

record.intro: A small residential service business evaluating Zanus AI should identify the phone-handling purchase separately from the rest of its software catalog. An owner who needs callers answered while working on a job may not need every front-office, back-office or automated outreach function presented beside the receptionist.

sections.title: Identify AI Phone before comparing the larger catalog
paragraphs:
The [Zanus AI Phone page](https://zanusai.com/fo/ai-phone.html) describes incoming answering, approved business knowledge, department-specific instructions and transfers to staff. Its wider navigation also includes tools for quoting, contacts, marketing and other office work. A feature appearing elsewhere in the catalog does not establish its inclusion in the phone subscription you select.

The [Front Office pricing page](https://zanusai.com/fo/pricing.html) links to Front Office and AI Server products. The live price table was not available as readable text in this review, so this guide supplies no verified dollar tariff or allowance. Obtain the current selected offer directly rather than relying on an older comparison or a price attached to a different product.

Ask for the exact product, enabled functions, usage unit and recurring commitment in one proposal. Do not compare an entire office-software package with a reception plan solely because both pages mention answering calls.

sections.title: Distinguish a transfer recipient from a phone operator
paragraphs:
Zanus makes a useful product-specific distinction: a colleague receiving a forwarded call on an existing phone is different from an operator using a phone extension inside Front Office. Confirm which arrangement each person needs and how it affects the selected offer. This guide does not establish the current price of either arrangement.

Write down what your office needs after an AI conversation reaches its limit. Does an available employee receive a transfer, does the caller leave a request, or is another supported next step offered? Ask how the person accepts the handoff and what happens when they do not accept it. A destination number alone does not establish an available recipient.

For a service owner moving between jobs, the important demonstration is an unavailable person as well as a successful connection. Keep the office's callback responsibility visible instead of assuming the receptionist has resolved the customer's request.

sections.title: Complete this AI Phone purchase card
paragraphs:
Use the card to obtain evidence for the particular Zanus offer you are considering. These are original evaluation questions, not a list of functions guaranteed in every subscription.

| Requirement | What to confirm in the selected offer | Evidence to inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business answers | Which approved source supplies a service or hours answer? | A sample answer and its accepted source |
| Incoming request | Which details are collected for a residential service inquiry? | The resulting record sent to the office |
| Appointment | Does the action request a time or confirm a supported booking? | The authoritative appointment record and confirmation boundary |
| Staff handoff | Is the recipient a forwarding target or an internal operator? | An accepted transfer and its accompanying context |
| Unavailable person | What happens when nobody accepts? | The supported fallback and named follow-up owner |
| Instruction change | Who approves an edit before it affects calls? | The accepted instruction and the observed caller response |
| Additional office work | Is quoting, outbound contact or another task separately enabled? | A specific scope, authority and charging definition |

Keep unanswered fields unresolved and use fictional requests for the demonstration.

sections.title: Test an unanswered question and a proposed rule change
paragraphs:
Zanus describes its phone product as working from approved knowledge and supporting staff handoff. Treat those descriptions as matters to verify in the account proposal and demonstration, not as proof that every answer will be correct.

Use a fictional homeowner asking about a service your business does not offer. Check whether the proposed workflow preserves that uncertainty and reaches the appropriate next step. Then provide an authorized change to ordinary office hours and ask how it becomes effective. Compare the caller's answer with the accepted instruction.

This is different from asking whether a website was imported. The business needs to know which information the active phone flow uses and who may change it. The separate [knowledge-base guide](/ai-answering-service/ai-receptionist-knowledge-base) explains the general source-review process; this purchase card connects that question to the selected Zanus phone arrangement and staff roles.

sections.title: Keep additional automation outside the reception comparison
paragraphs:
The AI Phone product page also advertises outbound and other office actions. Those can require a different task, permission and operating arrangement from receiving an incoming service inquiry. Do not assume they are needed, included or appropriate simply because they appear in the same product tour.

For example, a caller asking to discuss an existing estimate can be recorded for an authorized employee. That does not itself authorize a revised quote, a repeated outbound campaign or a change to a customer record. Identify which role would own any later action and verify the suitable arrangement separately.

This guide establishes no legal compliance conclusion for an outbound workflow, no technical connection to a particular field-service system and no on-premises phone deployment. It evaluates a reception purchase, not the full set of advertised office applications.

sections.title: Where Revo fits in the comparison
paragraphs:
Revo publishes AI answering, business-script intake, supported appointment booking and call summaries. Team transfers depend on the selected plan and supported configuration. Use [current Revo plans](/pricing) to verify the incoming-call scope your service business actually needs.

This page does not establish a Revo connection to Zanus, a Front Office operator panel, a back-office suite, outbound campaigns, automatic quote preparation or an on-premises server product. Compare the required reception outcomes and retained staff work, rather than treating all advertised software categories as equivalent.

sections.title: Questions before buying
paragraphs:
### Is every Zanus Front Office function part of AI Phone?

# Zanus AI receptionist for a small service business: choose the phone scope

A small residential service business evaluating Zanus AI should identify the phone-handling purchase separately from the rest of its software catalog. An owner who needs callers answered while working on a job may not need every front-office, back-office or automated outreach function presented beside the receptionist.

Published by Revo, a competing AI answering provider. This documentary guide uses Zanus public product pages reviewed October 28, 2026. It is not a hands-on performance test, an endorsement or evidence that either provider supports every task your business needs.

## Identify AI Phone before comparing the larger catalog

The [Zanus AI Phone page](https://zanusai.com/fo/ai-phone.html) describes incoming answering, approved business knowledge, department-specific instructions and transfers to staff. Its wider navigation also includes tools for quoting, contacts, marketing and other office work. A feature appearing elsewhere in the catalog does not establish its inclusion in the phone subscription you select.

The [Front Office pricing page](https://zanusai.com/fo/pricing.html) links to Front Office and AI Server products. The live price table was not available as readable text in this review, so this guide supplies no verified dollar tariff or allowance. Obtain the current selected offer directly rather than relying on an older comparison or a price attached to a different product.

Ask for the exact product, enabled functions, usage unit and recurring commitment in one proposal. Do not compare an entire office-software package with a reception plan solely because both pages mention answering calls.

## Distinguish a transfer recipient from a phone operator

Zanus makes a useful product-specific distinction: a colleague receiving a forwarded call on an existing phone is different from an operator using a phone extension inside Front Office. Confirm which arrangement each person needs and how it affects the selected offer. This guide does not establish the current price of either arrangement.

Write down what your office needs after an AI conversation reaches its limit. Does an available employee receive a transfer, does the caller leave a request, or is another supported next step offered? Ask how the person accepts the handoff and what happens when they do not accept it. A destination number alone does not establish an available recipient.

For a service owner moving between jobs, the important demonstration is an unavailable person as well as a successful connection. Keep the office's callback responsibility visible instead of assuming the receptionist has resolved the customer's request.

## Complete this AI Phone purchase card

Use the card to obtain evidence for the particular Zanus offer you are considering. These are original evaluation questions, not a list of functions guaranteed in every subscription.

| Requirement | What to confirm in the selected offer | Evidence to inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business answers | Which approved source supplies a service or hours answer? | A sample answer and its accepted source |
| Incoming request | Which details are collected for a residential service inquiry? | The resulting record sent to the office |
| Appointment | Does the action request a time or confirm a supported booking? | The authoritative appointment record and confirmation boundary |
| Staff handoff | Is the recipient a forwarding target or an internal operator? | An accepted transfer and its accompanying context |
| Unavailable person | What happens when nobody accepts? | The supported fallback and named follow-up owner |
| Instruction change | Who approves an edit before it affects calls? | The accepted instruction and the observed caller response |
| Additional office work | Is quoting, outbound contact or another task separately enabled? | A specific scope, authority and charging definition |

Keep unanswered fields unresolved and use fictional requests for the demonstration.

## Test an unanswered question and a proposed rule change

Zanus describes its phone product as working from approved knowledge and supporting staff handoff. Treat those descriptions as matters to verify in the account proposal and demonstration, not as proof that every answer will be correct.

Use a fictional homeowner asking about a service your business does not offer. Check whether the proposed workflow preserves that uncertainty and reaches the appropriate next step. Then provide an authorized change to ordinary office hours and ask how it becomes effective. Compare the caller's answer with the accepted instruction.

This is different from asking whether a website was imported. The business needs to know which information the active phone flow uses and who may change it. The separate [knowledge-base guide](/ai-answering-service/ai-receptionist-knowledge-base) explains the general source-review process; this purchase card connects that question to the selected Zanus phone arrangement and staff roles.

## Keep additional automation outside the reception comparison

The AI Phone product page also advertises outbound and other office actions. Those can require a different task, permission and operating arrangement from receiving an incoming service inquiry. Do not assume they are needed, included or appropriate simply because they appear in the same product tour.

For example, a caller asking to discuss an existing estimate can be recorded for an authorized employee. That does not itself authorize a revised quote, a repeated outbound campaign or a change to a customer record. Identify which role would own any later action and verify the suitable arrangement separately.

This guide establishes no legal compliance conclusion for an outbound workflow, no technical connection to a particular field-service system and no on-premises phone deployment. It evaluates a reception purchase, not the full set of advertised office applications.

## Where Revo fits in the comparison

Revo publishes AI answering, business-script intake, supported appointment booking and call summaries. Team transfers depend on the selected plan and supported configuration. Use [current Revo plans](/pricing) to verify the incoming-call scope your service business actually needs.

This page does not establish a Revo connection to Zanus, a Front Office operator panel, a back-office suite, outbound campaigns, automatic quote preparation or an on-premises server product. Compare the required reception outcomes and retained staff work, rather than treating all advertised software categories as equivalent.

## Questions before buying

### Is every Zanus Front Office function part of AI Phone?

Do not infer that from shared navigation. Obtain the selected product and enabled functions in the actual proposal, including the usage and staff-role definitions.

### Does a staff mobile receiving transfers need the same arrangement as an internal operator?

Zanus describes them separately. Confirm how your selected offer handles each role and obtain the current terms rather than assuming the same entitlement or charge.

### Why are no Zanus prices listed here?

Its live pricing table was not available as readable text in this review. A current proposal is needed; this guide does not substitute a third party's historical prices or another product's terms.

[Review Revo's current plans](/pricing) with the completed purchase card and identify which reception tasks the supported setup can demonstrate.
